note: Single source of truth for every controlled vocabulary on the site. Read by src/consts.ts (through the Astro build) and by tools/*.mjs (through src/lib/taxonomy.mjs). Nothing else may define these lists. This file exists because the same enum lived in four places - consts.ts, content.config.ts, two copies inside qa-check.mjs, and a prose list in MASTER_PROMPT.md - and they drifted. See docs/验收报告_第一阶段_2026-10-26.md.

categories.label: World
categories.description: What is happening beyond Malaysia's borders — geopolitics, conflict, international institutions and the shifts that set the weather for everyone else. Every piece here still ends with what it means for Malaysia; a world story with no Malaysian consequence does not get published.

categories.label: Malaysia Impact
categories.description: The same events read from the Malaysian side: what changes for jobs, prices, businesses, students and households here. This is the site's home column — the reason the other columns exist.

categories.label: Economy & Trade
categories.description: Trade rules, energy, commodities, inflation and employment — the numbers that end up in a Malaysian wallet, a Malaysian payroll or a Malaysian invoice.

categories.label: Tech & AI
categories.description: Where technology is going and what it does to work, learning and the tools Malaysian businesses and students will have to use — explained without the vendor language.

categories.label: Work, Education & Family
categories.description: The part of the world that lands at the kitchen table: which jobs are changing and what they now ask for, what education is worth and what it costs, and how households absorb a shift they did not choose. Written for the parent, the student and the worker rather than for the ministry that announced it.

categories.label: Business Opportunities & Risks
categories.description: Where a Malaysian firm can move and where it can be hurt: market access, supply-chain position, competition, regulation and financing. Every claim names the mechanism and the exposure — an opportunity with no named buyer and a risk with no named channel are both left out.
